preconditions.expression: all(c in {'#', '.'} for c in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each line of input (after the first) is a string P consisting only of '#' and '.' characters.
The first line of input is a positive integer T (number of test cases), followed by T lines of strings P.
Each string P has length at least 1.

preconditions.expression: all(P[0] == '#' and P[-1] == '#' for P in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The first and last characters of each string P are '#'.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.
Each output line is a non-negative integer representing the number of days.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(out) <= len(P) for P, out in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1:], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is a non-negative integer not exceeding the length of P.

postconditions.expression: all(int(out) == max(0, len([i for i in range(1, len(P)) if P[i] == '.' and (i == 1 or P[i-1] == '.')])) for P, out in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1:], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: The output for each test case is the number of days required to cross the passage, where each day corresponds to learning a new maximum jump length equal to the first encountered gap (sequence of '.') greater than the current maximum jump length (starting at 1).

postconditions.expression: all(int(out) == 0 if all(c == '#' for c in P) else int(out) >= 1 for P, out in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1:], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: If the passage has no gaps (all '#'), the output is 0. Otherwise, the output is at least 1.
